# The ground rules

One line per rule, and the link to the rule that owns it. Generated from `docs/rules/` by `python tools/rules.py --render`.


## Errors

- **An error propagates as a checked return, never by unwinding** — Every compiled function and every runtime helper carries one signature, and errors travel in its return value:… ([`errors/propagation`](rules/errors.md#errors-propagation))
- **A runtime helper never unwinds, and a panic dies inside one request** — Because nothing may unwind through a JIT frame, a runtime helper is declared `extern "C"` — never `extern "C-unwind"` — and wraps its body in `catch_unwind`, turning a panic into `FATAL` with the message recorded in `Ct… ([`errors/helper-abi`](rules/errors.md#errors-helper-abi))
- **A throw costs no more than a return, and allocates nothing** — The marginal cost of `errors/propagation`'s status check is **0.85 ns per frame**, measured as the slope between a 2-frame and an 18-frame chain so the harness's own call-out overhead cancels. ([`errors/throw-is-not-slower`](rules/errors.md#errors-throw-is-not-slower))
- **A limit report is not a Throwable, and the type checker knows it** — The `Throwable` classes are global and are the ordinary `catch` target. ([`errors/throwable-hierarchy`](rules/errors.md#errors-throwable-hierarchy))
- **A failure escalates through four tiers, and no tier is retried** — Nothing Novis runs is silently dropped, but not everything is *caught* — those are different guarantees. ([`errors/escalation-ladder`](rules/errors.md#errors-escalation-ladder))
- **Tier 1 — a resource limit reaches the request that spent it** — `Core\Fatal::onLimit(closure(LimitReport): void $handler): void` fires only for a resource-limit `FATAL` — memory, CPU time, `max_output`, wall time, `max_script_depth` and call-stack depth. ([`errors/on-limit`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-limit))
- **Recursion is bounded twice: a catchable error, then a fatal** — Novis compiles natively, so every user call is a real machine frame. ([`errors/stack-depth`](rules/errors.md#errors-stack-depth))
- **Tier 2 — an uncaught throw reaches the request root as itself** — `Core\Fatal::onUncaughtThrow(closure(Throwable): void $handler): void` fires when an ordinary `THROWN` propagates through every frame uncaught and reaches the isolate or request root. ([`errors/on-uncaught-throw`](rules/errors.md#errors-on-uncaught-throw))
- **Tier 3 — the configured handler is an ordinary isolate on the engine's own budget** — `[log] handler = 'path/to/handler.nvs'` names a script invoked as an ordinary `spawn script` isolate — fresh arena, fresh globals, its own config overlay, sharing nothing but compiled code — receiving one explicit repor… ([`errors/handler-script`](rules/errors.md#errors-handler-script))
- **Tier 4 — the floor is native, bounded, and gives up rather than escalating** — Hardcoded in Rust, with no script execution — there is nothing left here that could throw, panic or need a further tier, because this is the floor. ([`errors/engine-floor`](rules/errors.md#errors-engine-floor))
- **An internal panic never runs the failing request's own code** — A resource-limit `FATAL` means the *script* asked for too much. ([`errors/panics-bypass-user-code`](rules/errors.md#errors-panics-bypass-user-code))
- **A compile failure is catchable mid-execution and reaches the ladder at entry** — the chance to register anything. ([`errors/compile-failure`](rules/errors.md#errors-compile-failure))
- **One write path, and the engine floor is its other caller** — Application code and `errors/handler-script` call this; it is a thin binding over the **same native record-and-write helper** `errors/engine-floor` calls directly when it has no script to run at all. ([`errors/log-write`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-write))
- **Every developer-facing output is one closed record** — Every developer-facing output in Novis is a **record**: an envelope plus a tree of **nodes**. ([`errors/diagnostic-record`](rules/errors.md#errors-diagnostic-record))
- **Five levels, and the mapping to syslog is fixed** — An ordinary enum, and the syslog mapping is fixed — 7, 6, 4, 3, 2 — because `syslog` is a `errors/engine-floor` target and a severity is not optional there. ([`errors/log-level`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-level))
- **The sink in force picks the rendering, and no call site may name one** *(designed)* — A record is rendered as **plaintext**, **HTML** or **JSON**, and the sink already in force picks which. ([`errors/renderings`](rules/errors.md#errors-renderings))
- **Redaction, control bytes, bidi and elision are decided in the record** — Four transformations are properties of the **record**, applied when it is built, before any rendering sees it. ([`errors/record-transformations`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-transformations))
- **Five producers build the one record** *(designed)* — Five producers build `errors/diagnostic-record`, and none of them implements a format:… ([`errors/record-producers`](rules/errors.md#errors-record-producers))
- **A dump goes to the log, and reaches a response body only in development** — CLI dumps go to stderr, not stdout, so piping and redirection keep working while debugging. ([`errors/debug-dump`](rules/errors.md#errors-debug-dump))
- **A class cannot change how it is dumped** — There is **no customization hook**: no `DebugRepresentable`, no `__debugInfo`, no per-class renderer. ([`errors/no-render-hook`](rules/errors.md#errors-no-render-hook))
- **A record's fields are named and typed, not a stringly bag** — `fields` is a **named, typed** structure inside `errors/diagnostic-record`, never `array<string, mixed>` at the core. ([`errors/log-fields`](rules/errors.md#errors-log-fields))
- **Ambiguous input is refused whole, never repaired** — An input is **ambiguous** when two conforming readers can disagree about what it says. ([`errors/ambiguous-input-refused`](rules/errors.md#errors-ambiguous-input-refused))
- **The closed list of what makes an HTTP message ambiguous** — Refused on a request Novis receives **and on a response Novis's outbound client receives**:… ([`errors/http-message-defects`](rules/errors.md#errors-http-message-defects))
- **A cookie name is bytes, and a prefix is enforced once** — `Core\Request::cookie(name)` matches **byte for byte**. ([`errors/cookie-name-bytes`](rules/errors.md#errors-cookie-name-bytes))
- **A multipart body is capped by part count, not only by size** — `[limits] max_multipart_parts` defaults to **1000**, beside a per-part field-name length and a per-part size. ([`errors/multipart-part-count`](rules/errors.md#errors-multipart-part-count))
- **A path component that does not spell what it resolves to is refused, on every platform** — `Core\IO::within` — the launderer, and the one place the base directory is known — refuses a component that… ([`errors/path-component-refusals`](rules/errors.md#errors-path-component-refusals))

## Enums

- **An enum declares a new, closed, named integer type** — `enum Status { Active, Banned }` declares a new named integer type with a fixed set of cases, and the enum's name is then a type like any other — a property, a parameter, a return, a local, a class constant, an `array<T… ([`enums/closed-integer-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-closed-integer-type))
- **A case with no written value counts on from the one before it, starting at zero** — An enum body is a comma list of `Name` or `Name = <integer literal>`, and the optional `: int` or `: uint` before it names the backing type (`enums/one-backing-type`):… ([`enums/declaration`](rules/enums.md#enums-declaration))
- **PHP's `case` keyword does not parse, and each one is diagnosed where it is written** — There is no `case` keyword in an enum body. ([`enums/no-case-keyword`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-case-keyword))
- **Every enum is backed by exactly one integer type, and nothing else backs one** — `enum E: int` and `enum E: uint` name the backing type; with no `: T` written it is `int`. ([`enums/one-backing-type`](rules/enums.md#enums-one-backing-type))
- **A case is an integer constant, and an enum body declares nothing but cases** — `EnumName::CaseName` **is** an integer constant, inlined at every use site the way a literal `5` is: nothing is allocated, nothing is refcounted, there is no descriptor, and there is no per-isolate storage slot for an e… ([`enums/no-class-machinery`](rules/enums.md#enums-no-class-machinery))
- **An enum value costs nothing beyond the integer it is** — An enum value is its backing integer and nothing more — zero additional bytes over what `int` or `uint` already costs, no allocation, no refcount, no descriptor. ([`enums/representation`](rules/enums.md#enums-representation))
- **Reflection describes an enum's shape and grants it nothing a class has** *(designed)* — `Core\Reflect\EnumInfo::of(Status::class)` reports an enum's shape as ordinary structural metadata — the type's name and its closed case list — the same way `ClassInfo` reports a class's shape. ([`enums/reflection`](rules/enums.md#enums-reflection))
- **An enum case is always truthy, whatever integer backs it** — An enum case in a condition is **always truthy**, whatever integer backs it. ([`enums/truthiness`](rules/enums.md#enums-truthiness))
